title: Open Appeals and Added Review Time on Prior Authorization Deadline Extensions
content:
**Rule.** The appeal addition of a member-requested deadline extension looks at the member's appeals that are filed, acknowledged or under review: where one is about a prior authorization denial, two days are added; where none is about a prior authorization denial but one is about a claim denial, one day is added; otherwise nothing is added.

The appeals are the member's Appeals and Grievances cases whose status is filed, acknowledged or under review, read by their subject. The days are added once to the days a member-requested deadline extension on a Prior Authorization request adds, before the limits of one day and of the class's most review-extension days are applied.

| Open appeals (filed, acknowledged or under review) | Days added |
|---|---|
| at least one about a prior authorization denial | 2 |
| none about a prior authorization denial, at least one about a claim denial | 1 |
| neither | 0 |

## Training questions

**Q: The member has one open appeal about a prior authorization denial and one about a claim denial. What is added?**
A: 2 days. An open appeal about a prior authorization denial gives the addition of two days.

**Q: The member has two open appeals, both about claim denials. What is added?**
A: 1 day. The number of claim-denial appeals does not change the addition.

**Q: The member's appeal about a prior authorization denial has been decided and is no longer filed, acknowledged or under review. Does it count?**
A: No. Only appeals that are filed, acknowledged or under review are read.
